item1_fixture.reasoning: ok-docket is a synthetic stand-in for a model-backed run and its C1 is a mechanically-checked fact (note.txt exists, sha256 matches); CONFIRMS is exactly the standing the model path emits, and U5.22's rule is that CONFIRMS requires producer=='model'. The three alternatives are worse: (i) downgrade C1 so it renders EXTENDS would silently drop the suite's CONFIRMS-rendering and verify.ok=true coverage (behaviour change beyond this item); (ii) 'fixture'/'replay' producer would make a docket NAMED ok-docket fail verification, i.e. a lying fixture; (iii) inventing a distinct 'mechanically-verified' standing is a behaviour/design change (api.py prose-only, STOP-and-report boundary). A fixture whose name promises validity must be valid, so producer='model' is the right and honest value here. No second deliberately-invalid fixture is needed: the suite already covers a corrupt-but-present manifest (broken-docket: build then corrupt; direct build gives ok=false, and tests/test_dashboard.py:311 asserts broken verify.ok is False) and a no-verification-ran store-only entry (tests/test_dashboard.py:1465 asserts verify.ok is None). Both non-valid states already have coverage, so adding a fixture would be scope creep.
